title: Three Different EU Rules Are Making Ships Change Fuel Near Europe — and Only One of Them Is the ETS
standfirst: The EU ETS is a cap-and-trade system: a shrinking annual emissions ceiling, tradeable allowances worth one tonne of CO2 each, and a market-set carbon price that covered operators must pay if they don't cut emissions. Maritime transport was folded into it from 1 January 2024, covering all ships of 5,000 gross tonnage and above entering EU ports, regardless of flag . Coverage is asymmetric by voyage

title: To Comply or Not to Comply: CBAM Costs Indian Steel €93 a Tonne With Verified Data and €270 Without. Indian Carbon Credits Won’t Close the Gap
standfirst: India sent the EU USD 6.3 billion of CBAM-covered goods in 2024, most of it steel. Under the rules in force, verified emissions data cuts the 2026 charge on Indian hot-rolled coil from about €270 a tonne to €93. India’s own carbon credits, expected at €6–13 a tonne and not yet traded, are not recognised by the EU and would deduct little if they were.

title: Under CORSIA's Own Numbers, Corn Ethanol Fails as Jet Fuel — Worse Than the Fossil Fuel It Would Replace
standfirst: Under CORSIA's own default carbon-intensity tables, corn/maize ethanol converted to jet fuel scores worse than the fossil fuel it is meant to replace. India's ethanol policy has been actively promoting maize as a feedstock since November 2023. The two facts sit on a collision course that neither programme's own paperwork resolves.

title: Who Collects India's GST, and Who Actually Gets It Back
standfirst: Five states — Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Haryana — generate more than 40% of India's domestic GST.
